events.title: Haskell language published
events.summary: On April 1, 1990, the [Haskell] Committee published version 1.0 — a standard functional language built around mathematical-style programming.
events.about: [Haskell] treats programs as expressions rather than step-by-step mutations — popular in academia, quantitative finance, and as a testbed for language ideas that later appeared in Rust, Scala, and Swift. Its main compiler, [GHC], became the reference for research and production [Haskell].

narrative.whyChosen: [Haskell] unified many competing research languages into one teachable, widely studied design.
narrative.whyImportant: It popularized powerful type and abstraction ideas that later spread into mainstream languages.
narrative.problemSolved: Dozens of incompatible functional research languages existed; the community needed one common design to build tools and textbooks around.
